messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing weird cluster-autoscaler behavior in eu-west this morning. GPUs are highly fragmented across AZs: lots of nodes sitting at 10–25% GPU usage while pending single-GPU pods trigger new node launches in other AZs.

devon: I saw that too in canary last night. CA seems to prefer new nodes instead of packing. What expander are we using there?

liam: For some clusters we set `--expander=binpacking`, others `--expander=most-pods`. Problem is topology/affinity: pods request single GPU and we have AZ affinity constraints, so CA ends up choosing a node that increases AZ spread.

ashley: Can you paste the CA flags from the cluster? Also would be useful to compute a quick fragmentation metric (idle_gpus / total_gpus).

maya: current flags in staging (snippet):
```
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.2
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
--scan-interval=10s
```

k8s-bot: Deploy triggered: rollout/ca-tuning-config v2 -> staging

devon: `least-waste` sometimes picks a different instance type that has more free CPU/GPU slots but increases fragmentation across AZs. I prototyped a scoring tweak: score = free_gpus - (fragmentation_penalty * az_spread). It biases towards filling nodes in the same AZ.

liam: Could also try per-AZ node groups (so CA prefers binpacking inside an AZ) or a pre-filter that rejects scale-ups that increase AZ spread beyond a threshold.

ashley: :thumbsup: I'll run a 48h trace sim on Monday to compare current policy vs: (a) per-AZ binpack, (b) fragmentation-penalty patch, (c) lower unneeded-time. Will report numbers.

maya: One more thing — scale-down safety is sticky because a mix of PDBs + local-storage prevents eviction, so low-util GPU nodes remain. Maybe set `--max-empty-bulk-delete=10` and cautiously lower `--scale-down-unneeded-time` for gpu node pools only.

sre-oncall: Be careful lowering unneeded time — increases churn and possible OOMs during spikes. Run cost + reliability sim before changing production.

kevin: I opened RH-3421 with the CA decision logs, kube-scheduler traces, and a flamegraph. Assigned to @devon. Also added a Grafana panel for `gpu_fragmentation_ratio` and an alert at 0.25 so we can measure impact.

devon: Plan of attack: 1) small CA scoring patch in a staging build that applies fragmentation_penalty; 2) spin up per-AZ GPU node pools and set `--expander=binpacking` there; 3) run trace sim (ashley) and cost comparison. I'll open a config PR for staging.

maya: If we can avoid spinning up extra GPUs for the same workload we should save ~25–35% on instance cost. Also keeps tail latency lower.

ashley: Follow-ups: run sim (ashley), config PR + patch (devon), alert tuning (kevin). I put them in the sprint.

k8s-bot: CI: config PR passed lint + unit tests

sre-oncall: If the staging results look clean, let's bake to staging through Friday low-traffic window and monitor.

kevin: Added a quick query for historical fragmentation:
```
SELECT hour, SUM(idle_gpus)/SUM(total_gpus) as frag
FROM gpu_node_metrics
WHERE cluster = 'eu-west'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 48
```

devon: I'll update RH-3421 with the simulation outputs and a candidate PR link. Expect an update by EOD tomorrow.

maya: Thanks all. Hoping this reduces wasted GPUs and prevents unnecessary scale-ups.
